skill.name: upstash-redis-js
skill.description: Guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Upstash Redis development with TypeScript and JavaScript, including data structures, caching, search, transactions, and performance.
skill.summary: Build serverless Redis features with practical Upstash JavaScript and TypeScript guidance.
skill.author: upstash

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by JavaScript template literals, Redis pipeline exec methods, environment-based configuration, and search keyword fields. One static network finding is confirmed because the skill directs agents to provision an external database. Semantic review also found an authentication bypass placeholder and an unsafe simple lock-release example.

remediation.issue: The session example includes a credential verifier that accepts every login.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a non-executable interface or a function that throws until real password verification is implemented.

remediation.issue: The skill permits agents to provision a temporary database without explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before any provisioning POST, and explain the destination, lifetime, and returned credentials.

remediation.issue: The simple lock example releases locks without checking an ownership token.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the simple release pattern or use the token-checked Lua release for every lock example.

semantic_findings.title: Authentication Placeholder Accepts Every Login
semantic_findings.description: The verifyCredentials helper returns a user for every email and password. Copying this example into an application would create a complete authentication bypass.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper unconditionally returns a user object and never checks the password. The placeholder label is clear, but the executable example remains unsafe if adopted.

semantic_findings.title: External Database Provisioning Lacks Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells an agent to create a temporary Upstash database when credentials are absent. It does not require explicit user approval before the external POST.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction explicitly targets agents and describes a POST that creates a database. No confirmation or consent boundary appears in the instruction.

semantic_findings.title: Simple Lock Release Can Delete Another Owner's Lock
semantic_findings.description: The simple release function deletes a lock without verifying ownership. An expired and reacquired lock can be removed by the previous worker.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The finally block always calls redis.del through releaseLock. The same guide later provides token-checked release logic, confirming ownership validation is required.

content.user_title: Build Serverless Redis Features with Upstash
content.value_statement: Serverless Redis work requires correct command patterns, serialization, expiration, and concurrency choices. This skill provides focused Upstash Redis guidance for implementation, migration, search, and optimization.
actual_capabilities: Configures the Upstash Redis client with explicit credentials or environment variables.
Explains strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams, and JSON commands.
Builds caching, session, rate limiting, leaderboard, and distributed lock patterns.
Demonstrates pipelines, transactions, automatic batching, and server-side Lua scripts.
Guides migrations from node-redis and ioredis to the Upstash JavaScript SDK.
Covers Upstash Redis Search schemas, queries, filters, aggregations, aliases, and adapters.
limitations: Examples require an Upstash Redis database or another compatible connection for documented adapters.
The skill provides guidance and examples, not a runtime Redis service or deployment system.
Some examples need production authentication, validation, monitoring, and failure handling.
Upstash Redis Search guidance is not interchangeable with standard FT.SEARCH syntax.

output_examples.input: Create a cache for user profiles with a one-hour lifetime.
output_examples.output: A cache-aside design with namespaced keys, one-hour expiration, database fallback, and explicit invalidation after profile updates.

output_examples.input: Reduce latency for fetching profile data for many users.
output_examples.output: A pipeline strategy that batches related reads, preserves result ordering, and defines handling for partial failures.

output_examples.input: Add product search with price and category filters.
output_examples.output: An Upstash Redis Search plan covering schema fields, exact category matching, numeric price filters, pagination, and index readiness.

best_practices: Keep Redis credentials in environment variables and never place tokens in source code.
Namespace keys and apply expiration rules that match each data lifecycle.
Use token-checked locks and production libraries for concurrency-sensitive workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not treat all Redis values as strings when native serialization is available.
Do not use unbounded keys or sessions without expiration and cleanup rules.
Do not provision external resources or execute destructive commands without explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill create a Redis database?
faq.answer: It provides setup guidance. Any external database creation should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which languages does the skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on TypeScript and JavaScript with the Upstash Redis SDK.

faq.question: Does it support node-redis and ioredis?
faq.answer: It includes migration guidance and Redis Search adapters for both TCP clients.

faq.question: Can it help with Redis Search?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Upstash Redis Search schemas, queries, filtering, aggregation, aliases, and index management.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: They are educational patterns. Production systems still need authentication, validation, monitoring, and tested failure handling.

faq.question: How should credentials be supplied?
faq.answer: Use the documented environment variables or approved secret management. Never place real tokens in prompts or source files.
